chunks: When you faced them He made (the enemy) seem few to you in numbers, and made you appear fewer in their eyes, (it was) so that God could accomplish what had been decreed; for all things rest with God.

key_terms.أَمْراً کَانَ مَفْعُولاً: A decree that had been destined
key_terms.يُرِيکُمُوهُمْ: He made them appear to you

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of God making the enemy seem few to the Muslims at Badr?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine manipulation of perception (khawf) to ensure the Muslims' victory at Badr despite their numerical inferiority, serving as a test of faith and a fulfillment of the decree (amr maful). It underscores that ultimate authority and the outcome of all affairs belong solely to Allah, reinforcing the concept of divine sovereignty over historical events.
